title: Checking Existence of Edge Length Limited Paths
summary: Given an undirected graph with nodes connected by edges of specific distances, determine for each query if there exists a path between two specified nodes where all edges have distances strictly less than a given limit.
statement: Given an undirected graph with nodes connected by edges of specific distances, determine for each query if there exists a path between two specified nodes where all edges have distances strictly less than a given limit. Return a boolean array indicating the result for each query.
constraints: Undirected weighted graph; each query is [source,target,limit].
A valid path uses only edges with weight strictly less than limit. Return answers in query order.
hints: Queries become incremental connectivity checks when sorted by their limits.
Sort edges by weight and queries by limit; union every edge strictly below the current limit.
For each indexed query, advance the edge cursor, compare roots, and store by original query index.
The union-find contains exactly the graph induced by eligible edges, so shared roots are equivalent to an allowed path.
